name: Detective's Kit
text: This leather satchel contains empty vials, a pair of tweezers, a supply of small linen cloths, a set of brass calipers and a knotted string for measuring distances, several pieces of chalk, a pen, and a blank notebook for keeping notes. Every component of a detective's kit is of exceeding quality, and thus a detective's kit adds a +1 item bonus to checks to investigate a crime scene, a clue, or similar details. Like other tool kits, a detective's kit uses one hand if wearing the kit and two hands otherwise.
openQuestion: The kit names no skill — it says only "checks to investigate a crime scene, a clue, or similar details". Should it star EVERY skill plus Perception (as written here), or be narrowed to a short list (Perception, Society, Medicine, relevant Lore) to avoid putting a star on every row of the skill list?

name: Fishing Tackle (Professional)
text: This kit include a collapsible fishing pole, fishhooks, line, lures, and a fishing net. Professional fishing tackle grants a +1 item bonus to checks to fish.
openQuestion: The item names no skill — only "checks to fish". Survival (Subsist) is the usual home, but Fishing Lore / Sailing Lore are equally valid at many tables. Mark Survival only, or also lore:fishing?

name: Staff of Elemental Power
text: This staff is tapered at the base and carved into a gem-studded twist at the top. While wielding the staff, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to identify elemental creatures. **Activate** Cast a Spell --- **Effect** You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list. - **Cantrip** Frostbite - **1st** Breathe Fire, Pummeling Rubble, - **2nd** Blazing Bolt, Resist Energy **Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of all listed ranks of all listed spells.
openQuestion: The text names no skill ("checks to identify elemental creatures"). I mapped it to the skills the creature-identification table gives for elementals (Arcana and Nature). Confirm that pair, or prefer a single 'all skills' marker phrased 'to identify elemental creatures'?

name: Verdant Staff
text: This oak branch grows leaves in spring that change color in autumn and shed in winter. While wielding it, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to identify plants and fungi. --- **Activate** Cast a Spell **Effect** You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list. - **Cantrips** Tangle Vine - **1st** Runic Body, Runic Weapon - **2nd** Entangling Flora, Oaken Resilience, One with Plants, Shape Wood --- **Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of all listed ranks of all listed spells.
openQuestion: The text names no skill. Nature is the skill used to Recall Knowledge about plants and fungi, so I mapped it there - confirm, or should this also mark other skills a GM might allow (e.g. a relevant Lore)?

name: Gravedigger's Call
text: This rusted shovel functions as a *+2 striking decaying glaive* when wielded as a weapon, but it more closely resembles a neglected tool. Its haft was carved from the trunk of a long-dead tree that once grew among the broken stones of an abandoned cemetery, and its blade was forged from shattered remnants of the armor that failed to protect those buried there. When you carry or wield a *gravedigger's call*, you gain a +1 item bonus to Perception checks to seek options=gravediggers-call haunts and to skill checks to determine the reasons for a haunt or spirit's existence. --- **Activate—Call the Fallen** ⟨2⟩ (concentrate, manipulate) **Frequency** once per day **Effect** You cast Rouse Skeletons as a 5th-rank occult spell. The DC is 30. --- **Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of *rouse skeletons* (5th rank).
openQuestion: The second half of the bonus is "+1 item bonus... to skill checks to determine the reasons for a haunt or spirit's existence" without naming a skill. Which skills should carry that star - Occultism and Religion only, or every skill the GM might allow (Society, Lore, etc.)? I will not guess a skill list the text does not state.

name: Standard Astrolabe
text: **Activate—Calculate** 1 minute (manipulate) --- Astrolabes can be used for navigation in unfamiliar or featureless locations. To use an astrolabe, the holder must be trained in Survival. By spending 1 minute to measure the height of the stars and planets, a holder who knows the time and date can determine the latitude, and a holder who knows their latitude can determine the date and time. An astrolabe also grants a +1 item bonus to checks to identify celestial bodies. A standard astrolabe functions only on steady ground.
openQuestion: The text never names the skill used to "identify celestial bodies" — it only requires Survival training to use the astrolabe. Attach the +1 to Survival only (what I did), or also to Astronomy Lore / Nature, or to 'all' skills with the condition text carrying the restriction?

name: Mariner's Astrolabe
text: **Activate—Calculate** 1 minute (manipulate) --- Astrolabes can be used for navigation in unfamiliar or featureless locations. To use an astrolabe, the holder must be trained in Survival. By spending 1 minute to measure the height of the stars and planets, a holder who knows the time and date can determine the latitude, and a holder who knows their latitude can determine the date and time. An astrolabe also grants a +1 item bonus to checks to identify celestial bodies. A standard astrolabe functions only on steady ground. A mariner's astrolabe contains additional stabilizers that make it suitable for use on moving surfaces, such as the deck of a ship.
openQuestion: Same as standard-astrolabe: which skill key should "checks to identify celestial bodies" hang on — Survival (my choice), an Astronomy-style Lore, or 'all'?

name: Combat Fishing Pole
text: The combat fishing pole is a sturdy and flexible pole that can be used as a weapon in melee. When a lure is attached to a combat fishing pole, it can be used to make thrown weapon attacks with a range increment of 20 feet, though the lure must then be reeled back in with an Interact action before the weapon can be used at range again (see the tethered trait). The ranged trip, tethered, thrown, and versatile P traits of the combat fishing pole only apply to thrown attacks made with a lure; throwing the pole itself leaves you with no practical way to retrieve it other than moving to its location and picking it up. A combat fishing pole can be used alongside fishing tackle to fish, and it adds its item bonus from weapon potency runes (if any) as an item bonus on checks to fish when used in this manner.
openQuestion: "Checks to fish" names no skill — should this map to Survival (the Subsist/fishing skill), to Fishing Lore, or be left unassigned?

name: Astrolabe of the Falling Stars
text: This astrolabe is fashioned of magically attuned platinum plates and rings and is inset with carefully measured ruby gems. The astrolabe's back is engraved with helpful charts, a calendar, and a maker's mark. An astrolabe of falling stars can be used as a Mariner's Astrolabe. In addition, it can produce the following magical effect. --- **Activate—Starfall** ⟨1⟩ (manipulate) **Frequency** once per day **Effect** With a flick of your finger, you set the astrolabe's rule spinning, causing the inset rubies to become a blur. Choose a point within 100 feet. The astrolabe of falling stars calls down a brief rain of meteorites in a centered on that point, dealing damage to creatures in the area ( save). --- **Activate—Calculate** 1 minute (manipulate) Astrolabes can be used for navigation in unfamiliar or featureless locations. To use an astrolabe, the holder must be trained in Survival. By spending 1 minute to measure the height of the stars and planets, a holder who knows the time and date can determine the latitude, and a holder who knows their latitude can determine the date and time. An astrolabe also grants a +1 item bonus to checks to identify celestial bodies.
openQuestion: Which skill does "checks to identify celestial bodies" map to — Survival (implied by the Survival-training requirement in the same paragraph), Astronomy Lore, or should it stay unassigned?
